current_sota.description: v7 architecture with 40 interaction features, no mirror augmentation

top_15_archs.name: v8_PairformerCrossSym
top_15_archs.core_change: Add explicit 5×5 pair representation matrix; update via triangle multiplication (Pairmixer) to capture all sym-triplet interactions
top_15_archs.key_math: pair[i,j] += sum_k gate(pair[i,k]) * pair[k,j]; triangle captures (i,k,j) transitivity
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: Different from basic GAT/MHSA: maintains dedicated pair matrix updated via triangle multiplication — fundamentally new information structure

training_hooks.notes: pair matrix init from outer product of encoded sym pairs; triangle update in 1-2 passes

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: Init pair[i,j] = Linear(cat(z_i, z_j)); triangle update with gate: split d_pair into [gate|value], compute outer product sum

top_15_archs.name: v8_SPOPlusLoss
top_15_archs.core_change: Replace MSE loss with SPO+ listwise ranking loss that directly optimizes cross-sectional PnL ranking; optionally DFF two-stage: pretrain MSE then fine-tune with SPO+ in trust region
top_15_archs.key_math: L_SPO+ = -sum_i softmax(y_i/T) * log softmax(pred_i/T); T=0.1 temperature; L_total = alpha*L_MSE + beta*L_SPO+
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: This is a training objective change, not architecture — completely orthogonal to all rejected architectures

training_hooks.notes: Start with alpha=0.7, beta=0.3; warm up MSE for first 20 epochs then add SPO+ loss; use DFF trust region if unstable

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: def spo_loss(pred, y, T=0.1): return -(y.softmax(dim=-1) * pred.log_softmax(dim=-1)).sum(-1).mean()

top_15_archs.name: v8_VIME_MaskSSL
top_15_archs.core_change: Add mask estimation auxiliary loss to existing SAE: single linear head predicts which features were corrupted; BCE loss forces encoder to learn feature covariance structure
top_15_archs.key_math: mask_head: Linear(d_latent=64, n_feat=259); L_mask = BCE(sigmoid(mask_head(z)), mask); L_total = L_pred + 0.3*L_recon + 0.1*L_mask
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: mask_ssl (basic) was rejected — that was purely reconstruction without mask estimation. VIME adds MASK PREDICTION as second SSL task, fundamentally different signal

training_hooks.forward_signature: def forward(self, x, mask=None): # returns pred, _last_recon_loss, _last_mask_loss
training_hooks.extra_inputs: mask: (B,5,259) bool tensor generated during training with p_mask=0.3
training_hooks.notes: Corrupt: x_corrupt = x.clone(); x_corrupt[mask] = x[random_other_samples][mask]; z = encoder(x_corrupt)

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: Add self.mask_head = nn.Linear(d_latent, n_feat) to existing model; generate mask before forward pass in trainer

top_15_archs.name: v8_T2GFeatureGraph
top_15_archs.core_change: Replace flat MLP per-sym encoder with T2G-Former: automatically estimates feature-to-feature relation graph, performs graph-guided attention over 259 feature tokens per sym
top_15_archs.key_math: R_ij = sigmoid(q_i^T k_j / sqrt(d)); attention A = softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d) + log(R)); z = A*V then mean-pool over 259 tokens
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: T2G-Former is a per-sym FEATURE encoder, not cross-sym attention. Entirely different layer from GAT (which was cross-sym). Works inside each sym before cross-sym step.

training_hooks.notes: Feature embeddings: embed feature ID (0..258) into d_emb=32; project scalar feature value to d_model=64 via Linear(1, 64); attention masked by learned graph R

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: 259 tokens per sym per sample — (B*5, 259, 64) self-attention. Use 4 heads, 2 layers. Mean-pool to get (B, 5, 64) per-sym latent.

top_15_archs.name: v8_SetNormCrossSym
top_15_archs.core_change: Replace LayerNorm in cross-sym attention with Set Norm: normalize each sym's representation RELATIVE TO OTHER SYMS (set-level mean/std), not independently
top_15_archs.key_math: SetNorm(z_i) = gamma * (z_i - mean_j(z_j)) / std_j(z_j) + beta; mean/std computed over 5-sym set; same params as LayerNorm but set-aware
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: Set Norm is a normalization strategy change, not an architecture. Replaces LayerNorm with cross-sym normalized version. Orthogonal to all rejected architectures.

training_hooks.notes: Also try: SetNorm on final pred head input; try both pre-norm and post-norm variants

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: class SetNorm(nn.Module): mean/std over dim=1 (sym dimension) instead of dim=-1 (feature dimension). Also apply equivariant skip connections: residual z_i = z_i + f_equivariant(z)

top_15_archs.name: v8_SCARFContrastive
top_15_archs.core_change: Add SCARF-style cross-sym contrastive loss: corrupt random features with marginal distribution samples; InfoNCE loss between clean/corrupted representations for same sym
top_15_archs.key_math: x_corrupt[mask] = x_rand_batch[mask] (not Gaussian); InfoNCE: L = -log(exp(sim(z_i, z_i_corr)/T) / sum_j exp(sim(z_i, z_j)/T)); T=0.1; positives=same-sym clean/corrupt
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: SCARF uses marginal distribution corruption (not Gaussian noise) and InfoNCE contrastive loss. Different from basic mask_ssl which only does reconstruction. Contrastive loss is the key addition.

training_hooks.forward_signature: def forward(self, x, x_corrupt=None): # x_corrupt generated in trainer
training_hooks.notes: Corruption: for each feature col, with prob p=0.6 sample from that col's empirical distribution across batch. Positive pairs: (z_clean_i, z_corrupt_i). Negatives: all other (sym, sample) pairs in batch.

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: In collate_fn or before forward: generate x_corrupt by randomly replacing 60% of features with batch-marginal samples. InfoNCE over flattened (B*5) embeddings.

top_15_archs.name: v8_DualAttnTLOB
top_15_archs.core_change: Add FEATURE self-attention (over d_latent dimension treating 5 syms as features) orthogonal to existing SYM self-attention; dual attention captures both cross-sym AND cross-feature dependencies
top_15_archs.key_math: Block: z -> sym-attn(z) -> transpose(d,N) -> feat-attn(z^T) -> transpose back; both attentions applied sequentially; each has 4 heads
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: TLOB dual attention is a fundamentally different operation from standard MHSA: it adds a TRANSPOSED attention (features attend over syms) that standard MHSA never computes.

training_hooks.notes: Feature attn: (B, d_latent, 5) — attend over 5 syms for each of d_latent features. Use 1 head (5 dim per head). After feat-attn, transpose back. Apply after sym-attn in same block.

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: class DualAttnBlock: sym_attn(z) then feat_attn(z.T).T; can stack 2 blocks total

top_15_archs.name: v8_DFFFineTune
top_15_archs.core_change: Two-stage: (1) pretrain v8 best model with MSE+recon as before; (2) fine-tune final 10 epochs with SPO+ loss subject to trust region constraint on weight change
top_15_archs.key_math: Stage 2: min L_SPO+(ŷ, y) s.t. ||theta - theta_0||_F <= epsilon; implemented via L2 regularization to theta_0: L_total = L_SPO+ + lambda_trust * ||theta - theta_0||_F^2
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: DFF is a POST-TRAINING fine-tuning strategy, not an architecture. Can be applied to any existing v8 model after MSE training.
top_15_archs.expected_pnl: +0.3 to +1.0 over SOTA (stacks on top of any v8 arch)

training_hooks.extra_inputs: save initial weights theta_0 after MSE training
training_hooks.notes: lambda_trust=0.01; fine-tune for 5-10 epochs; use lower LR (1e-5); monitor validation PnL not MSE

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: After main training: theta_0 = deepcopy(model.state_dict()); add ||theta-theta_0||_F * lambda to loss in fine-tune phase

top_15_archs.name: v8_ContextRoutedMoE
top_15_archs.core_change: Replace single per-sym MLP with 6 expert MLPs; routing from CROSS-SYM context (not per-sym input); top-2 routing; experts specialize in market regimes
top_15_archs.key_math: ctx = mean(cross_sym_attn_output); gate = softmax(W_r * ctx); top-2 experts activated; z = sum_{k in top2} w_k * expert_k(x_sym)
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: Previous v6_moe was BROKEN — it had sym-specific routing (violation of sym-agnostic constraint). This version routes from CROSS-SYM context, which is sym-agnostic and correct.

training_hooks.notes: Load balance: aux_loss = N_experts * sum(f_k * p_k) where f_k=fraction assigned, p_k=mean router prob. Prevents expert collapse. n_experts=6, k=2.

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: Experts: 6 × nn.Sequential(Linear(259,128), GELU, Linear(128,64)) — same size as existing per-sym encoder. Router: Linear(64, 6).

top_15_archs.name: v8_OmniGNNMarketNode
top_15_archs.core_change: Add learnable virtual 'market' node to 5-sym graph; all 5 syms connect to market node; 6-node GAT enables O(1) information propagation (any sym can influence any other in 1 hop)
top_15_archs.key_math: nodes = cat(z_syms, z_market); z_out = GAT(nodes, full_adjacency)[:5]; z_market = learnable Parameter(d) initialized to zeros
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: Basic GAT was rejected as 'borderline' (v6). OmniGNN adds virtual market node which is fundamentally different: it creates a star topology where all syms communicate through a shared hub, not pairwise.

training_hooks.notes: Initialize market node embedding randomly; it gets updated via backprop as a global context absorber. Can also try: market node = mean(z_syms) (no extra params).

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: Market node added as 6th token in MHSA: z6 = market_embed.expand(B,-1,-1); full_z = cat([z_syms, z6], dim=1); after MHSA, take only first 5

top_15_archs.name: v8_CRISPAdaptGraph
top_15_archs.core_change: Learn sparse adjacency matrix A (5×5) from per-sym features; A = sigmoid(MLP(cat(z_i,z_j))); sparse via top-k masking; GNN message passing on learned graph
top_15_archs.key_math: A_ij = sigmoid(W_e * cat(z_i, z_j) + b); A_sparse = top_k(A, k=3) per row; msg_i = sum_j A_sparse[i,j] * z_j; z_i' = z_i + msg_i
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: Basic GAT uses fixed attention weights from QK^T. CRISP learns EDGE EXISTENCE (0/1) separately from edge weights, then applies explicit sparsity — different design.

training_hooks.notes: Sparsity reg: L1 on A matrix. Alternative: Gumbel-softmax for differentiable top-k. Try k=2 or k=3 neighbors.

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: Edge predictor: Linear(d_latent*2, 1) applied to all 5*5=25 pairs; sparse via top-k or threshold

top_15_archs.name: v8_SEChannelGate
top_15_archs.paper: SENet (Hu et al. CVPR 2018) adapted for cross-sym 2024
top_15_archs.core_change: Add SE-style channel excitation gate after cross-sym MHSA: squeeze to global context, excite to per-sym importance weights; ultra-lightweight (500 extra params)
top_15_archs.key_math: ctx = mean(MHSA_output, dim=1); gate = sigmoid(FC2(relu(FC1(ctx)))); shape: d->d/4->5; z_out = MHSA_output * gate.unsqueeze(-1)
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: SE-Net is a gating mechanism added ON TOP of MHSA output — not a replacement. Different from all rejected architectures.

training_hooks.notes: Stack after cross-sym MHSA. Also try SE over feature dimension (within per-sym encoder): squeeze d_latent to 1, then excite back to d_latent.

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: class SEGate(nn.Module): FC(d,d//4) -> ReLU -> FC(d//4, 5) -> sigmoid; 500 params total

top_15_archs.name: v8_SAINTDualAttn
top_15_archs.core_change: Implement SAINT dual attention: alternate between feature-wise attention (within each sym's 259 features) and sym-wise attention (across 5 syms); explicit 2-stage interaction
top_15_archs.key_math: Stage 1: per-sym (B*5, 259, d) self-attention over features; Stage 2: cross-sym (B, 5, d) self-attention over syms; repeat L=2 times
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: SAINT alternates feature AND sample attention — current v7/v8 only has sym-attention. The per-sym feature attention is a completely new component.

training_hooks.notes: Feature attention uses feature tokens: embed feature ID (0..258) + project scalar value to d_model. Keep num_feature_tokens=32 (use PCA or random projection to reduce 259→32 feature tokens) for efficiency.

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: Two transformer blocks: FeatureAttn(B*5, n_feat_tokens, d) then SymAttn(B, 5, d). Stack 2 times.

top_15_archs.name: v8_FactorGraphEncoder
top_15_archs.core_change: Build dynamic cross-sym graph from FACTOR SIMILARITY (cosine similarity of encoded sym features); soft adjacency A_ij = cos_sim(z_i, z_j); GNN message passing on this dynamic graph
top_15_archs.key_math: z = encoder(x); A_ij = dot(normalize(z_i), normalize(z_j)); msg_i = sum_j softmax(A_ij) * z_j; z_out_i = z_i + W * msg_i
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: GRU-PFG builds graph from FACTOR FEATURES (not price returns, not fixed adjacency). Dynamic per-sample adjacency based on how similar syms' current features are — fundamentally different from static GAT.

training_hooks.notes: Differentiable: A is softmax of cosine similarities. No extra learned params for edge weights (dynamic, from data). Message proj W: Linear(d, d).

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: z_norm = F.normalize(z, dim=-1); A = bmm(z_norm, z_norm.T); msg = bmm(softmax(A), z); z_out = z + Linear(msg)

top_15_archs.name: v8_ReMaskerPretext
top_15_archs.core_change: Replace/augment current Gaussian-noise reconstruction with ReMasker-style re-masking: randomly zero out 30% of features, reconstruct ONLY those features (not all); forces encoder to learn feature correlations from remaining features
top_15_archs.key_math: mask ~ Bernoulli(p=0.3); x_masked = x * (1-mask); z = encoder(x_masked); recon = decoder(z); L_recon = MSE(recon[mask], x[mask]) / mask.sum() (only masked positions)
top_15_archs.why_not_rejected: Current reconstruction uses Gaussian noise on ALL features. ReMasker completely zeros out random features and reconstructs only those — fundamentally different: encoder must infer missing features from context.

training_hooks.forward_signature: def forward(self, x, mask=None): # mask: (B,5,259) bool
training_hooks.extra_inputs: mask generated in trainer before forward
training_hooks.notes: In trainer: mask = torch.rand(x.shape) < 0.3; x_input = x * ~mask; call forward(x_input, mask); compute recon on masked positions only

top_15_archs.implementation_notes: Minimal change to existing model: change trainer to generate mask and pass masked input; change recon loss to only compute on masked positions

combo_recommendations.name: Combo A (lowest complexity, highest expected gain)
combo_recommendations.reasoning: All three are loss/norm changes requiring zero new architecture — can be stacked with ANY existing v8 model

combo_recommendations.name: Combo B (novel architecture + loss)
combo_recommendations.reasoning: Pairformer provides novel triplet interactions; SPO+ aligns training objective; VIME adds mask SSL

combo_recommendations.name: Combo C (comprehensive)
combo_recommendations.reasoning: T2G for per-sym feature graph; DualAttn for orthogonal cross-feature attention; SetNorm for relative normalization; DFF for decision-focused fine-tune

notes: All architectures maintain sym-agnostic constraint (no sym embeddings, no sym-specific params). All are compatible with existing (B,5,259) -> (B,5) interface. SPOPlusLoss and DFFFineTune can be applied on top of any architecture without code changes to the model class itself.
